Subject: Quick recap + proposed acceptance targets from today's call

Hi Jay / Ana —

Thanks again for the time today. Helpful discussion — summarizing the key performance points we captured and the proposed acceptance criteria so we can align the pilot: 

High-level ask from Elara: production-quality hosted inference with minimal changes to client stack, ability to sustain daytime throughput, and predictable tail latency for clinical workflows.

Proposed acceptance (initial):
- E2E (client SDK -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> client render) p95 <= 250ms for short-chat flows (average sequence length ~80 tokens)
- E2E p99 <= 550ms for the same workload
- Sustained throughput: 120 concurrent active sessions (approx 900 qps steady-state) with <5% error rate
- Streaming: chunk latency (time between first byte and first token) <80ms for streaming-enabled clients

Next steps I propose:
1) We'll run a focused p95/p99 qualification run using your sample traces + our synthetic burst tests. Plan attached (p95_p99_test_plan.xlsx).
2) Rishi to confirm kernel/quantization config and expected per-GPU throughput.
3) Agree on a 72-hour pilot window (we provision dedicated pool) and a mutual action plan / LoE.

Attachments: p95_p99_test_plan.xlsx (test cases & traffic shape), network-trace-sample-20261112.zip

If that looks good I'll schedule the pilot kickoff for Monday and loop in infra.

Thanks,
Monica

Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed acceptance targets from today's call

Monica —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few technical notes from the runtime team to set expectations for the qualification run: 

1) Workload assumptions — short chat flows (avg 80 tokens) map to batch sizing of ~8-16 per GPU depending on concurrency. We'll run both 8 and 16 batch configurations.
2) p95/p99 targets are achievable on the hosted stack with our current 48GB A100 equivalent pools if:
   - client-side concurrency patterns do not include sustained single-user spikes >20 simultaneous open streams
   - network RTT from Elara's region (us-west) stays under ~25ms to our hosted region
3) Streaming behavior — our SDK already supports chunked responses; first-token latency is typically dominated by decode and kernel launch when sequence length is small. We expect <80ms first-token in controlled tests; real-world could vary if network or client parsing is slow.

Action items from infra:
- I'll provide the kernel/quantization profile we'll use for the pilot by EOD Friday.
- Need the sample TLS handshake traces / CDN edge IPs from Elara so we can run realistic e2e RTT shaping.

I'll also add a conservative fallback configuration (slightly lower batch) to guard p99 spikes during warmup.

-rishi
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Monica / Rishi —

Appreciate the write-up. A few clarifications from our side so the pilot isn't a surprise: 

- Our real-world mix includes both short clinician prompts (~50–100 tokens) and longer note-generation flows (~600 tokens) when generating discharge summaries. For the pilot we can focus on the short prompts but need to understand how longer tails impact p99 under load.
- Network: our primary hosting is in us-west-2; median RTT to Redwood's region is ~18ms. We'll share CDN edge IPs and recent tcpdump snippets.
- Compliance: we need audit log evidence that pilot traffic is segregated and logs retained for 90 days. Please include a short compliance statement.

We can do the 72-hour window but want to lock down acceptance checks and an escalation path if p99 exceeds target during business hours. Also please provide an estimated cost delta for dedicated pool for the pilot.

Jay

Jay / Ana —

Thanks for the note and the extra detail. A few practical confirmations and what we'll deliver for the pilot: 

What Redwood will provide for the 72-hour pilot:
- Dedicated hosted pool (isolated) with monitoring and per-request tracing.
- Pre-agreed kernel/quant settings (Rishi to attach profile).
- A scripted test harness that replays your provided traces + synthetic bursts for 3 load patterns: steady-state, diurnal peak, and cold-warm startup.
- Compliance stub: isolated audit logs, retention 90 days, and an access log export. We'll share a short compliance statement PDF.

Acceptance checks during pilot (automated):
- p95 and p99 computed every 15 minutes across the accepted short-prompt test set
- If p99 > 600ms for two consecutive 15-minute windows during 9am–6pm PT, automatic rollback to a conservative serving config + alert to both teams
- Error rate threshold: >5% over a 30-minute window triggers investigation and pause

Cost & provisioning notes:
- Estimated incremental for dedicated 48GB pool for 72 hours: ~$4,200 (incl. monitoring and tracing) — this is a pilot estimate, final cost depends on exact concurrency and burst profile.

Next actions required from Elara:
1) Send the CDN edge IPs and tcpdump (Ana) — needed to shape RTT in our harness.
2) Approve the pilot MOP (Marcus will send as a one-pager).
3) Sign mutual action plan (DocuSign link will be sent).

I'll attach the compliance statement and the one-pager MOP in the next message.

—Vivek
